findings.claim: The new `access != WorkflowAccess::TerminalRecovery` exemption has no observable behaviour in unmutated source; it exists only to keep Issue41's mutation evidence independent. The causal-mutant section does not classify a mutant that removes the exemption, so an implementer could try to claim a kill for it.
findings.evidence: For TerminalRecovery, put_workflow_transition's conservative branch evaluates `attempt.session_id.is_some() || !attempt.dispatch_started` on before.history[before.active]. That runs before validate_transition and before the closure block. In every reachable state it rejects exactly the attempts the new predicate matches, because EvidencePort can never carry a marker. Removing the exemption therefore yields the same refusal, the same unchanged durable state and the same counters; only the error literal can differ. That is the Design1 all-access behaviour and is behaviourally equivalent. The exemption's value is that Issue41's single-Store-TR and combined Engine+Store TR mutants still produce a committed closure: unwrap_err() or is_err() fails on Ok. It does not change any decision itself.
findings.fix: Add one line to the mutant accounting. Removing the TerminalRecovery exemption is an equivalent mutant (no credit); the exemption exists only so that Issue41's TerminalRecovery mutants stay causal. Optionally re-execute those two Issue41 mutants under the new source and record that they still produce a committed closure.

review.assessment: I re-reviewed the Design2 delta against the unchanged source; the Design1 Medium and Lows are correctly resolved, and no design fault remains. (1) The TerminalRecovery overlap is resolved with option A. The new Store guard applies only to closures with access != TerminalRecovery. TerminalRecovery is still refused by its earlier conservative unbound-dispatch fence, which uses the same predicate on the same original attempt and runs before validate_transition. TerminalDecision never changes active, so it never enters the closure block. StateOnly, ReadOnly and Mutating closures, including same-generation retry, generation invalidation and index replacement, all reach the new guard. Every access mode therefore still refuses an unresolved marked-unbound closure, as requirement 2 demands. Issue41's evidence stays causal. With the conservative Store TerminalRecovery fence removed, the direct TerminalRecovery call on the held start passes validate_transition: Interrupted with a terminal decision, and the terminal-Task decision check holds. The closure block (now exempt for TerminalRecovery) finds no Session rows, so the transition commits and the existing unwrap_err() fails. With both TerminalRecovery fences removed, release_terminal_reservation succeeds and is_err() fails. No text-only credit is involved. (2) The shared literal makes Engine-only removal truly masked. retry's persist returns put_workflow_transition's error without added context, so the message is identical. Before refusal, the mutated path only reads the Session loop: no Lost row exists in the specified fixtures, and the matching-row fixture's Failed row is admitted. Durable state and counters are therefore identical. (3) The direct construction positives are feasible. The identical same-generation builder commits on a bound terminal Failed review rejection (own Exited reviewer Session, unrelated Exited executor row, predicate false), on a nonirreversible EvidencePort Waiting or Failed attempt, and on the pre-marker definitive Failed fixture. (4) The generation context is now precise. make_context uses next_phase(&invalidated), the first configured phase after invalidate clears completed; workflow.sources; the new generation; and latest+1. set_context-equivalent pointers satisfy validate_context and validate_transition (revision and context_version). (5) The pre-marker pauses 3 and 4 for both actors are safe and correctly assert only state and counters. At pause 3 refresh_owners fails on the Record version, release_preparation finds the claim changed, and nothing is written. At pause 4 the marker persist is rejected by validate_transition as an untyped generation-rewrite or history-immutability error, eligible stays false, and nothing is released or launched. (6) The stale-CAS priority note is accurate. The guard reads the DB's `before`, so only callers whose transition otherwise validates see an untyped refusal where they previously saw a Task/Record SnapshotChanged. No closure caller classifies typed errors. own_task_marker_rollback classifies only the marker persist, which keeps active. Issue41's TerminalRecovery tests, design and mutations are inventoried as consumers. No schema, API, bypass, certificate, producer, or whole-Issue14/native/F1/MVP claim is introduced. The one Low is mutation-accounting precision.

findings.claim: The new assurance that 'every access mode still refuses this unresolved closure' is causally exercised only for StateOnly (new guard) and TerminalRecovery (existing conservative fence). No control closes through ReadOnly or Mutating, so a mutant that narrows the new guard to `access == StateOnly` would survive every listed control.
findings.evidence: put_workflow_transition applies the closure block to every access mode. validate_transition does not limit closure by access mode, so a crate-private caller could close an active attempt with ReadOnly or Mutating. For ReadOnly/Mutating, the extra Session scan bails only on executor_reserved or Lost rows (and, for Mutating, any non-terminal row). The Executor held-start fixture has no Session rows, and the Reviewer fixture has only the Exited Implement Session, so both scans pass. TerminalDecision cannot close: the conservative branch requires expected == after apart from the decision, which keeps active. Every direct Store control the design lists uses StateOnly.
findings.fix: Add one direct Store closure refusal on the held marked-unbound Running fixture using WorkflowAccess::Mutating or ReadOnly (Executor suffices), with the full snapshot unchanged. Then record the 'guard only for StateOnly' narrowing as a killable mutant. Alternatively, record that narrowing as an executed survivor, without credit, for the raw-only access paths.

review.assessment: I checked the Design2 delta against the unchanged source; all Design1 findings are resolved. (1) D1-M1 resolved by option A. Exempting WorkflowAccess::TerminalRecovery from the new closure guard is sound. The conservative TerminalRecovery branch runs before validate_transition and the closure block, and enforces `session_id.is_some() || !dispatch_started` on the same `before.history[before.active]` attempt. That predicate matches the new guard because a marked EvidencePort attempt is impossible. TerminalRecovery is therefore still refused, and requirement 2 holds for that mode. TerminalDecision keeps active and never enters the closure block, and every other mode gets the new guard. Issue41's evidence becomes causal again with no text credit. Removing the single Store TerminalRecovery fence lets the direct TerminalRecovery call in preparation_dispatched_observation_and_direct_store_terminal_fence commit: no Session row exists during the held start, so own_found is true and unwrap_err panics. Removing both Engine and Store TerminalRecovery fences lets release_terminal_reservation commit, so its is_err assertion fails. (2) The mandatory shared literal makes Engine-only removal genuinely masked for every listed fixture. The Store ensure! error propagates through persist unchanged and without added context, durable state and counters are identical, and the design now bars message-based credit. (3) The generation builder is now exact. With next_phase(&invalidated), workflow.sources, the new generation, latest_context+1 and set_context-equivalent pointers, it satisfies validate_context (phase, generation, authority, revision) and the validate_transition generation branch, matching the existing unknown_gate builder. (4) The identical same-generation retry builder commits on all three fixtures. The bound review rejection (Failed via validate_evidence, Exited own Session, context phase ImplementationReview) passes the closure check and own_found. Port Waiting/Failed on Commit (non-irreversible, no own Session, Exited Implement row only) passes. The pre-marker unregistered-executor Failed fixture passes. In each case Waiting stays Waiting, completed_at is set only if absent, and the RetryEvent has the exact index, which satisfies the closing block. (5) The pre-marker pause behaviour holds at both offsets for both actors. At offset 3, refresh_owners fails on the Record version, and release_preparation then fails its claim or version check with no write. At offset 4, marker publication fails the untyped validate_transition (history immutability, or generation rewrite, for the generation builder) with eligible=false. Neither writes or launches, so comparing the post-closure raw snapshot and counters is the right actor-independent assertion. (6) The stale-CAS error priority and own_task_marker_rollback statements are accurate: the marker persist keeps active unchanged, and no closure caller classifies typed SnapshotChanged. The Issue41 TerminalRecovery tests, design and mutations are now listed as consumers. No schema, API, bypass, certificate or producer change is introduced, and the no-escape consequence and the open status of Issue14, native, F1 and MVP are preserved. The single Low is optional coverage precision for raw-only access paths; there are no blockers.
